simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to מַרְבֵּק (H4770) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: n-m.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: מַרְבֵּק (marbêq) means a stall (for cattle) First listed occurrence: 1Sam 28 24.

definitions.full: H4770. marbeq מַרְבֵק noun [masculine] stall (literally tying-place ); — מ מִתּוֺךְ ׳עֲגָלִים Amos 6:4 calves out of the stall (where they were fattened); ׳עֵגֶלמֿ 1Sam 28:24 i.e. a stall-fed, fatted, calf; so מ ׳כְּעֶנְלֵי Malachi 3:20 (simile of prosperity), Jer 46:21 (simile of well-fed and arrogant mercenaries).
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to tie up ;
